style: A bright, bold, slightly stylised 3D illustration in the look of a clean low-poly video game: clear sunny daylight, simple smooth shapes, saturated but natural colours, a deep blue sky with a few white clouds. Child-friendly and exciting, like a picture in a children's book about rockets. Landscape 3:2 composition. The real SpaceX Starship vehicle, drawn accurately: a very tall slender two-stage rocket made of shiny stainless steel; the upper stage (the ship) has a pointed nose, a black heat-shield side and four flaps, two small at the top and two large at the bottom; the booster below it is a plain steel cylinder with four grid fins near its top; the launch tower is a tall dark steel lattice tower with two long horizontal catching arms. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos, flags, symbols or wordmarks anywhere in the image, and no writing on the rocket, the tower, the trucks or the ground.
tileStyle: Square composition. One single bold subject, large and centred, filling most of the frame, with a simple uncluttered background and strong contrast, so the picture is readable as a small icon-like thumbnail. Very few small details.

facts.fact_biggest: The full Starship stack, ship on top of booster, standing upright on its launch pad and towering high above everything around it. Tiny trucks, a few tiny people and small palm trees at the foot of the rocket make its enormous size obvious. Low camera looking up so the rocket fills the height of the picture.
facts.fact_catch: View from the front, looking at the tall dark lattice launch tower in the background centre. Two long horizontal catching arms are attached to the tower and reach straight out towards the viewer, side by side, spread wide apart like a pair of open tongs. Between the two arm tips, in the gap, the Super Heavy booster hovers upright in mid-air with no ship on top: a plain stainless-steel cylinder with a flat top and four grid fins, no black side, no nose cone, no flaps. Bright orange rocket flames pour from its engines at the bottom with a little smoke. Both arms are complete, solid and connected to the tower. Blue sky.
facts.fact_engines: The bottom of the Super Heavy booster seen from directly below and slightly from the side, looking up at its flat base. The base shows exactly three concentric rings of rocket engines: 3 engines in the centre, a ring of 10 engines around them, and an outer ring of 20 engines, all clearly separated, all firing with bright orange and yellow flames streaming down towards the viewer. Steel body of the booster curving away above, blue sky behind.
facts.fact_mechazilla: Side view of the very tall dark lattice launch tower, drawn big, with its two long horizontal arms (the chopsticks) attached to the tower and reaching out sideways to the right, one above the other, both complete, solid and connected to the tower, stretched wide open like giant robot arms. The shiny Starship rocket stands upright on its pad beside the tower, just beyond the tips of the arms. Camera slightly low, blue sky.
facts.fact_starbase: A wide view of a launch site on a flat sandy coast: the Starship rocket standing on its pad with the dark lattice launch tower beside it, a few low white buildings and tanks, a sandy beach and the blue sea with gentle waves stretching to the horizon on one side, flat green-yellow grassland on the other. Warm sunny day.
facts.fact_steel: A close-up of the shiny stainless-steel hull of the Starship, filling the whole picture: a smooth curved mirror-like steel wall made of stacked rings, with thin horizontal weld seams between the rings, reflecting the blue sky and white clouds. Bright sunlight and soft highlights on the polished metal.
facts.fact_starlink: Outer space with the curved blue Earth below. A long line of flat rectangular Starlink satellites, each with one large dark blue solar panel, flying in a row across the picture in orbit above the Earth. From the satellites soft glowing light beams reach down through the thin atmosphere to a small cosy house and a little town with lit windows on the Earth below. The picture contains no rocket and no launch tower; only satellites, Earth, the house and the town.
facts.fact_heat: The Starship ship falling belly-first through the upper atmosphere with its black heat-shield side facing the viewer and glowing bright orange and yellow, wrapped in a fiery orange and pink plasma sheath that streams away behind it. Its four flaps are spread out. The blue curved Earth far below with white clouds. The picture contains no launch tower, no booster and no ground buildings; only the ship, the plasma, the sky and the Earth below.
facts.fact_bellyflop: The Starship ship, stainless-steel with a black side, falling horizontally through the sky belly down like a skydiver, with its four flaps spread wide like arms and legs. The sky is blue with white clouds, and far below the launch site with a tiny tower on a flat coast and the sea can be seen.

tiles.stage_mission: The whole journey in one picture: a Starship rocket rising from a tiny launch site at the bottom, leaving a long curving bright trail of flame and smoke up into the dark blue of space, with the curve of the Earth and a few stars at the top.
tiles.stage_liftoff: The full Starship stack lifting off its pad right beside the dark lattice launch tower, huge orange flames and big white clouds of steam billowing out at the bottom. Low camera, blue sky.
tiles.stage_maxq: The Starship rocket high in the sky, punching upwards through a flat layer of white clouds, with a big white vapour collar ring wrapped around its body, and several large glowing golden rings of light floating in the sky ahead of it above, to fly through. Deep blue sky. There is no launch tower, no launch pad and no ground buildings anywhere; at most the sea and a faint distant coastline far below through gaps in the clouds.
tiles.stage_staging: Very high in the sky, in the deep blue near the edge of space with the curved Earth far below and no tower and no ground nearby. The Starship booster (plain steel cylinder with four grid fins) and the ship above it are splitting apart, with a clear gap between them filled by a big bright ring of orange and yellow fire and sparks. Both pieces are large and clearly visible, vertical, seen close up.
tiles.stage_catch: The Super Heavy booster, a plain stainless-steel cylinder with four grid fins and no ship on top, descending upright between the two long arms of the dark lattice launch tower, with orange engine flames below it. Front view, the arms spread wide on both sides.
tiles.stage_deploy: The Starship ship stands upright in the frame, nose pointing up, seen from above and to one side, with the large bright curved Earth filling the background behind and below it, black starry sky on the other side. Low on the ship's side is a wide, low, horizontal slit, and flat Starlink satellites slide straight out of it sideways, away from the ship, one after another. Each satellite is a large, long, flat, dark slab lying like a tray, perpendicular to the ship's long axis: its broad flat top face points up towards the sun and is lit by bright sunlight, with a few small bright white lights on it; it is very thin in the direction of the ship's length. One tray is half out of the slit, and one or two more trays have already drifted away below and beside the ship in a line, clearly visible against the bright Earth. The trays are completely flat with nothing unfolded, no wings and no panels sticking out. Make the trays big in the frame. The ship floats alone in space: there is no launch tower, no launch pad, no ground, no booster and no buildings anywhere; the bottom of the ship is cropped by the lower edge of the frame, and everything below is only the Earth far away. The trays are very large, each nearly as wide as the ship is tall in the frame, thick enough to see their edge, with a crisp bright sunlit top face and a bright glint on it so they stand out strongly from the Earth.
tiles.stage_reentry: The Starship ship falling belly-first, its black heat-shield side facing the viewer and wrapped in glowing orange and yellow plasma flames streaming behind it, flaps spread. Dark blue sky above, the Earth below.
tiles.stage_shipcatch: Front view of the very top part of the dark lattice launch tower, high in the sky. The tower's two long arms are near the top of the tower and are spread on both sides, closed gently around the Starship ship in the middle, holding it upright at its sides: the ship alone, large, showing its pointed nose, black belly side and four flaps, with a small orange flame under its engines. Below the ship there is only open blue sky and white clouds, and the ground is tiny and very far below, barely visible.
